street_smart.title: You park your two-wheeler outside a shop for 'just a couple of minutes' without locking the steering, and when you get back, it's gone. What do you do first?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation topic (two-wheeler theft prevention) — no single matching incident in today's feeds, and every other rotation topic (digital-arrest scams, UPI fraud, cab/auto overcharging, rental traps, fake job offers, OTP scams, medical emergency response, tenant/landlord rights, consumer court, phone snatching, loan-app harassment, card skimming) has been used as a street-smart scenario within the last 3 weeks of archived briefs.
street_smart.situation: It's been a few minutes, there's no CCTV visible on the shop itself, and a couple of bystanders say they didn't notice anything. You need to decide what to do right now, not after the trail goes cold.

choices.text: Call the nearest police station or dial 100 immediately to file an FIR with the bike's registration, engine and chassis numbers, then check nearby shops/ATMs for CCTV footage.
choices.feedback: Correct. An FIR is the single most important step — it's required for any insurance claim, and it lets police act fast while the trail is fresh. Keep your RC and insurance papers handy (or a photo of them) so you have the numbers on hand instantly.

choices.text: Wait a day or two assuming it'll turn up, since filing a police report feels like a hassle.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Delaying the FIR gives the thief more time to move or resell the vehicle, and most insurers require police intervention within a short window of the theft — waiting can cost you the claim entirely.

choices.text: Post about it on local social media groups asking people to help track down the bike, and go looking for it yourself with friends.
choices.feedback: Crowdsourcing tips isn't wrong, but confronting a suspected thief yourself is dangerous and can complicate the police case. Report to police first and let them lead any recovery — share tips with them, not by chasing leads on your own.

choices.text: Assume it's a lost cause and just start looking to buy a replacement.
choices.feedback: Skipping the report means no insurance payout and no chance of recovery — Bengaluru police do recover a meaningful share of reported two-wheeler thefts, but only for cases that are actually filed.

takeaways: Always lock the steering (and use a secondary chain/disc lock for a few extra seconds of deterrence) even for 'just a minute' stops.
File an FIR the moment you notice the theft — it's mandatory for an insurance claim and most useful while the trail is fresh.
Keep a photo of your RC and insurance papers on your phone so you have the registration, engine and chassis numbers ready instantly.

quiz.question: What disrupted train services on the Mangaluru-Bengaluru route in today's news?
quiz.why: Landslips are common on this route during the monsoon because the line cuts through the Western Ghats' steep, rain-soaked terrain.

quiz.question: Kannada outfits have called for a Karnataka bandh on which date, amid the Cauvery water-sharing row?
quiz.why: The Cauvery dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu dates back over a century and has repeatedly triggered bandh calls during periods of water stress.

quiz.question: Per today's news, how many people has the Kerala Chief Minister confirmed dead so far in the state's heavy rains?
quiz.why: Kerala's hilly terrain and monsoon intensity make it especially prone to landslides and flash floods during heavy spells like this one.

quiz.question: Which of these states does NOT share a border with Karnataka?
quiz.why: Karnataka borders six states in all — Maharashtra, Goa, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala — but not Odisha, which lies further east along the coast.

quiz.question: Which vitamin does the human body synthesize when skin is exposed to sunlight?
quiz.why: UVB rays trigger vitamin D synthesis in the skin, which is why brief daily sun exposure is often recommended alongside dietary sources.
